definitions.gloss: seal of approval; firm guarantee; confident endorsement
definitions.explanation: Originally referred to a large round seal resembling a drum. Now used figuratively to mean a strong personal guarantee or confident recommendation, typically in the expression {太鼓判|たいこばん}を{押|お}す.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}が{太鼓判|たいこばん}を{押|お}した。
examples.english: The teacher gave a seal of approval.

examples.japanese: {品質|ひんしつ}には{太鼓判|たいこばん}を{押|お}せる。
{料理長|りょうりちょう}が{太鼓判|たいこばん}を{押|お}した{新|しん}メニューだから、ぜひ{食|た}べてみてください。
examples.english: The head chef has given this new menu item his seal of approval, so please try it.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used in the set phrase {太鼓判|たいこばん}を{押|お}す (to stamp one's seal of approval, to guarantee with confidence). The expression implies the speaker is putting their personal reputation behind the endorsement.

ETYMOLOGY:
Originally referred to the large, round gold coins ({大判|おおばん}) of the Edo period that bore a prominent round seal ({判|はん}) resembling a drum ({太鼓|たいこ}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {太鼓判|たいこばん}を{押|お}す (to give one's seal of approval)
- {太鼓判|たいこばん}{付|つ}き (guaranteed, endorsed)
